subject: WHEN-COMPILED function
notes: cite.py --check 15.99.3 "The character positions returned, numbered from left to right, are" => OK §15.99.3 1) (Returned value rules). PATH READ END TO END: IntrinsicRenderer.cs:871 `"WhenCompiled" => EmitText.CsLiteral(WhenCompiledStamp.Value)` inside RenderStringValue; WhenCompiledStamp (line 45) = `RuntimeApi.DateFormat21(IntrinsicBinder.CompileClock())`; RuntimeApi.cs:965 `DateFormat21(DateTimeOffset t) => CobolDate.Format21(t)`; CobolDate.cs:33 Format21 = `t.ToString("yyyyMMddHHmmssff", InvariantCulture) + (t.Offset >= TimeSpan.Zero ? "+" : "-") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours).ToString("00") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Minutes).ToString("00")`. This is the SAME formatter CURRENT-DATE uses (§15.21.3's table is character-for-character the same table), which is why this row inherits that row's open owner question rather than getting an independent verdict. POSITION BY POSITION AGAINST THE RULE TEXT: 1-4 four Gregorian year digits - InvariantCulture pins the proleptic Gregorian calendar and ASCII digits, "yyyy" zero-pads to four; 5-6 "MM" 01-12; 7-8 "dd" 01-31; 9-10 "HH" 00-23; 11-12 "mm" 00-59; 13-14 "ss" - conforms on BOTH LEAP-SECOND branches (cite.py --check 7.3.17.4 "the implementor defines whether a value greater than 59" => OK §7.3.17.4 GR2, which leaves the ON-phrase maximum implementor-defined, and .NET's DateTimeOffset cannot represent a 60th second so "ss" never exceeds 59; LeapSecondDirectiveProcessor's own summary records the REPORTED side as answered "never" for WHEN-COMPILED by name); 15-16 "ff" hundredths 00-99, and the '00 when the system has no fractional facility' escape is unneeded since DateTimeOffset.Now carries sub-second precision; 17 - '+' on `Offset >= TimeSpan.Zero` (correctly INCLUDING the 'same as UTC' boundary the rule assigns to '+') and '-' otherwise, with '0' unreachable, which is right because .NET always provides the local time differential factor; 20-21 `Math.Abs(t.Offset.Minutes)` two digits 00-59. NOTE ON THE TRANSCRIPTION: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 34038 renders position 17's minus as U+2013 EN DASH (verified by codepoint scan); the emitted character is ASCII hyphen-minus, which is the only dash in the §8.1.2 COBOL character repertoire - an OCR artifact, not a divergence. THE OPEN POINT, and the reason this is not CONFORMS: positions 18-19 require '00 through 13' when position 17 is '+', and `Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours)` is UNCLAMPED, so on a host whose local offset is +14:00 (Pacific/Kiritimati, 'Line Islands Standard Time' - a zone both Windows and IANA ship) the compiling host bakes '14' into positions 18-19. The standard's table offers NO in-range value for such a host, so no behavior conforms: emitting 14 is an out-of-range extension, clamping to 13 misreports the offset, and '0'/'00'/'00' asserts the false 'no facility' case. THIS IS ALREADY A REGISTERED OWNER QUESTION, NOT A NEW ONE: the inventory row RV-15.21.3-1 carries the identical finding and states 'the same unclamped expression also feeds WHEN-COMPILED (15.99.3, identical table)', and kb/Work/PB67.md (status: owner) closes with 'The separate CURRENT-DATE +14:00 spec-hole question (RV-15.21.3-1) remains its own decision'. D13 reserves the call to the owner. THE QUESTION THIS ROW CARRIED IS ANSWERED: on a host whose local UTC offset lies outside the rule's table, CURRENT-DATE and WHEN-COMPILED REPORT THE TRUE OFFSET. ONE DETERMINATION, BOTH ROWS: RV-15.21.3-1 and RV-15.99.3-1 share it because one formatter serves both (CobolDate.Format21) and §15.99.3 r1's table is character-for-character §15.21.3 r1's; the compile-time bake (IntrinsicBinder.CompileClock) and the run-time read (RunUnit.Current.Clock) are independent seams onto that one formatter, and the shared test asserts they agree rather than assuming it. WHY NO ALTERNATIVE CONFORMS: the rule caps positions 18-19 at 00..13 under '+' and 00..12 under '-' (cite.py --check 15.21.3 'two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13 indicating the number of hours that the local time is ahead of Coordinated Universal Time' -> OK; the same text --check'd against 15.99.3 -> OK), and for a +14:00 host the table names no value at all - emitting 14 leaves the range, clamping to 13 misreports what §15.21.1 defines as 'the ... local time differential factor provided by the system on which the function is evaluated' (--check -> OK), and '0'/'00'/'00' asserts position 17's 'the system ... does not have the facility to provide the local time differential factor' (--check 15.21.3 -> OK), which is false. Reporting the truth is the only option that states nothing untrue. DOCUMENTED per §4.2.6 ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK) and §4.2.7 (--check 'Language elements that an implementor may, but need not, implement are listed in A.4' -> OK), in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §3 as a named determination bullet. BOTH SIGNS, and the '+' one is a real host: IANA Pacific/Kiritimati = Windows 'Line Islands Standard Time' ('(UTC+14:00) Kiritimati Island' - read off the host zone table, not inherited); the '-' side is unreachable from any host zone but reachable through the WISEOWL_COBOL_CLOCK pin, which parses a DateTimeOffset directly and so admits -14:00. THE DEPARTURE IS BOUNDED, AND THE TEST PINS THE BOUND: CurrentDateOffsetDeterminationTests re-derives the whole §15.21.3 r1 position table from the rule text and requires the set of out-of-range position spans to be EXACTLY {18-19} across the fixtures and EMPTY for every offset the rule admits - so a regression that broke positions 15-16 or 20-21 at an extreme offset fails even while the headline value still looks right. End to end through the clock seam: CurrentDateOffsetPinTests runs a COBOL program under WISEOWL_COBOL_CLOCK at +14:00, -14:00, +13:00, +05:45, +00:00 and -09:30 and asserts all 21 characters.
